Techniques for tabletop miniature painting
description:
Today I bring you a video testing the new PlayMarkers from @akinteractive.official . Here is a brief explanation of the steps of this video and at the end some conclusions.

For this video I have chosen a really demanding and small miniature from the Warcrow Adventures board game.

1- We use the PlayMarker to give the base coats to all the surfaces of the miniature, we do it using different colours and taking advantage of the fact that this product covers very well. We can mix it in the palette so that the colour jump is not so evident.

2- Once we have applied the base coats, we apply a dry brush to outline all the edges quickly.

3- The key is to use washes to even everything out and also do the outlining in shadow, for this we can use products such as Deep shades, oil washes or something similar. First I wash by parts with different colours and then I do a general wash with black and purple Enamel, this will give harmony to the whole.

4-We do details like mud and blood with very simple techniques (dry brush or stippling).

This product IS NOT: For expert painters looking for maximum precision or very detailed work.

This product IS: To apply base coats easily, it has a paint with good dilution and covers great, it is also very resistant. It is for painters looking for something simple and clean. I also think it is ideal for children.
——————————————————————————-
Hoy os traigo un video probando los nuevos PlayMarkers de @akinteractive.official . A continuación una breve explicación de los pasos de este vídeo y al final unas conclusiones.

Para este video he elegido una miniatura realmente exigente y pequeña del juego de mesa Warcrow Adventures.
1- Usamos los PlayMarker para dar las capas base a todas las superficies de la miniatura, lo hacemos usando diferentes colores y aprovechando que este producto cubre muy bien. Podemos mezclarlo en la paleta para que el salto de color no sea tan evidente.

2- Una vez hemos dado las capas base aplicamos pincel seco para perfilar todas las aristas de una forma rápida.

3- La clave está en usar lavados para emparejar todo y que ademas haga el perfilado en sombra, para ello podemos usar productos como las Deep shades, lavados de óleo o algo similar. Primero hago lavado por partes con diferentes colores y después hago un lavado general con Enamel negro y morado, esto dará armonía al conjunto.

4-Hacemos detalles como barro y sangre con técnicas muy sencillas (pincel seco o punteado)

Este producto NO ES Para pintores expertos que buscan la máxima precisión o trabajos muy detallados.

Este producto SI ES: Para aplicar capas base fácilmente, tiene una pintura con buena dilución y cubre muy bien, además es muy resistente. Es para pintores que buscan algo sencillo y limpio. También me parece ideal para niños.

title: PMP Final Submissions Changes
description:
Join us for a quick video on changes to the PmP Google+ Hobby Community. 

Currently, all final models are submitted as End of Month Submit.
All models are then reviewed each month in the End of Month review video. 
The growing number of submissions means that we cannot review each model in as much depth as we would like to. 
Going forward, the End of Month Submit tab will be split into two tabs. You only need to post in one tab. 
Finished Models: This category will be for the sharing of your finished pledges and work over the months. The community is encouraged to offer feedback and engage as normal, but this will not be reviewed on the monthly video. 
End of Month Review: This category will be for finished models you want reviewed in the End of Month video. This should be models which you have questions on, want in depth critiques for and/or feel represent a big step on your hobby journey. Be focused in your post as to your questions and we will seek to give targeted feedback. There is no hard limit on this, we are on the honor system, so please post responsibly.

title: Topic of the Week - The Fun Player
description:
For our topic this week, we turn to the Fun Player. We've all encountered the bad player, the smelly player, the rules bending player, etc... but what about the fun player? The guy who will 20-0 you but makes sure you still had a good time.  
Tell us what these players do during the games that make if fun? Is it just their personality? which personality traits make a player fun to have a game with? 
Is it just their energy aura? their positive vibe? Do they happen to be a stand up comedian and are just cracking jokes all the time? 
I want to know the secrets behind being a fun player so that we can all adopt one or two of these traits and make games more enjoyable for everyone!

Shoutout to Kyle Balombin (The Peacemaker) for the suggestion of the Topic of the Week.

description:

Wind Globadier/Grenadier Recipe: 

Backpacks on Maxmini site $7.89 + postage but there is someone selling 12 on EBay.com right now for $11 buy it now! Type in maxmini, they are the biohazard backpacks.
Veer-Myn Nightmare parts- loads on EBay.com from Hoard'o'bits, including one excellent listing with 30 heads! Combat arms alone, for the "open" hands were a couple of dollars. I got my Nightmares for £10 but would have used Hoard'o'bits if it existed in UK.
Stormvermin bodies and arms - I got mine cheap at a show a while back but again Hoard'o'bits will probably be your best bet.
 
Assembly is dead easy. Stick body together. Shave a little off of the back of the shoulder area to get a good contact point for the backpack - dry fit before gluing. Stick on the head. Stick on a left arm. Right arm - cut off the hand at the join in the armour. Repeat on the Veer-Myn arm. Glue together - easier to do this before gluing arm to the body. Then stick a BB pellet in the hand. You might want to slightly file down the inside of the hand for better contact points with the BB pellet. I also filed down the join line around the BB pellet.
 
Gluing the hand to the arm is a little fiddly, so once glued, set aside to give time to bond properly before gluing to the body. I always use superglue.
 
And there you go.

title: Mordheim: Age of Sigmar Alpha Rules Available
description:
Quick video to announce the release of our Mordheim: Age of Sigmar alpha rules set. 

Rules: https://www.dropbox.com/sh/2wtslxi5wm65li8/AAB6kZliBHc-OiuzxsAyoc3sa?dl=0

The link above contains everything you need to get playtesting in the newest version of the City of the Damned, including the rules, the warbands, the roster sheets and some quick play guides. 

Our hope is that with this set of rules, even those that may not have liked Age of Sigmar as a replacement to WHFB may like it as a new version of a small scale skirmish game, where the simple and fast rules combine with what we have added to make a compelling system to tell your story in the ruined city. 

Some Notes:
1) This is an alpha and we are releasing it now to gather as much feedback as possible from the community. We welcome all community feedback and will be setting up a formal method for collection soon. 
2) Don't worry about Spelling/Grammar and similar items, as well as page layout and those sorts of things. This is effectively Post-design, so we are well before the editing stage where that work would be done. 
3) If you want to know more or get prepped, Tom and I did a video - you can find that here (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uS6okP4ATc4).

title: Six Tips for your 1st game of Warhammer: Age of Sigmar
description:
In this video I talk through 6 tips I have found are helpful in having a fun, engaging first game of Age of Sigmar. I hope they help and I welcome you to share your feedback and tips below. 

Twitter: @warhammerweekly

1: Start Small - 4 Warscrolls - 1 monster, 1 hero, 1 unit, 1 warmachine
2: Play slow, read often
3: Discuss your choices and your unit's abilities
4: Try crazy stuff, use mystical terrain, push and kill some models
5: Don't agonize over your choices - just grab some scrolls and go
6: Don't change a bunch of rules - try it how it's written, it might surprise you!

title: Warhammer Topic of the Week - Women in Warhammer
description:
In this video I talk about the tender subject of Women in Warhammer and women in our lives. Our hobby has a very low female participation rate and I discuss some issues why that might be. I also talk about what our wives, girlfriends and significant others think about participation in the hobby. 

Questions: Why is there a low percentage of female participation? Does the aesthetic and narrative of warhammer (both of which are absent many females) have an impact? Does the male-oriented community of warhammer have a negative effect on female participation? What does your significant other think of your participation in the hobby?

As I mention in the video, this is a tricky conversation, but we are adults and I believe in our ability to have a reasonable, positive and respectful conversation about. All videos that meet that criteria will be linked below.

description:
Another video in what is becoming a series of videos where I tie together strange concepts and Warhammer 9th edition. In this video, I examine the Hueristic Bias' of Anchoring, Confirmation Bias and Negativity Bias and how they have made our experience of the coming of 9th edition sour. 

Behavioral Economics + Warhammer? Strap in the for the thrill ride.

Wiki Page Mentioned: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cognitive_biases

description:

description:

Post your comments and thoughts below, but please be respectful. I do not mean to insult anyone with these ideas and I welcome dissenting opinion.

title: On the Return of Warhammer Weekly
description:
Warhammer Weekly returns January 28th at 8pm EST. We have a full show lined up for you and we hope to see you there!

If you have questions or models to submit for us to review in the Q&A and Model review portions respectively, please submit them to vincentrventurella@gmail.com.

Can't wait to see everyone next week!

title: A Tale of 2 Changes - Major Changes in Games and 9th Edition Warhammer
description:
Why do some major changes in games succeed while others fail?In this video, I walk through two big changes in past games, Magic & D&D and try to figure out why one big change succeeded greatly, and one failed. 

Magic Article by Mark Rosewater: http://archive.wizards.com/Magic/magazine/article.aspx?x=mtg/daily/mm/259

4e D&D Early Review: http://geek-related.com/2008/06/06/dd-4es-out-and-its-awful-heres-why/

There are certainly many other great articles on these subjects with differing opinions, sadly I can not list them all here, but if you have one you like, feel free to list below.

title: 9th Edition Rumors Upsides
description:
In this video I take a few minutes to walk through what I think are the potential upsides of the rumors for 9th edition and try to find silver linings. I think there could be many (possible) great things about the changes and I walk through a few of them here.

TSC Vid: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6jr8MF7r37o

title: Warhammer End of Year Acceptance Award Speech
description: Thank you to everyone who voted for me for best conversion. I give my acceptance speech, show some models, and talk about the return of Warhammer Weekly with Woopy and myself in 2015.

description:
In this video I talk about the idea of making Rules free not just for the players, but also for the designers and what might happen if GW published Warhammer under an OGL similar to D&D 3.X. 

TSC Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i_oZ4ytIVlw

title: Warhammer Youtubers Grudge Match World Tour 2015
description:
Warhammer YouTubers World Tour Grudge Match 2015! A video wherein I challenge the Warhammer Youtubers community in a Road Trip Warhammer extravaganza. 

Email me at vincentrventurella@gmail.com if you are interested in me coming to a table near you this summer.

title: Warhammer Khaine & the Paradox of Choice
description:
Khaine Magic and the Paradox of Choice. I spend a few minutes walking through what I think the real danger of the Khaine magic phase is and how it could disrupt not only the game, but our feeling of self-worth while playing.

Link to the video I mention is here (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VO6XEQIsCoM)

title: Fun & Psychographic Profiles in Warhammer
description: Fun - What is it good for? A great deal, but what do we mean by fun. Today I am going to talk about Psychographic profiles in games and how fun is actually defined.

title: Balance & Warhammer
description: Balance - Like a Double Rainbow, what does it mean. I take some time to walk through the concept of Balance in Warhammer and what it really means when you ask for Balanced rules.

title: We Gotta Sell Something! - The Games Workshop Conundrum
description: Come with me on a magical journey where I perform a little thought experiment to get inside the mind of GW and try to determine what they can do to sell us more stuff.

title: Why warhammer isn't sinking anytime soon
description: Some thoughts on the idea of the future of Warhammer and the idea of Warhammer as a "sinking ship." Long story short - I talk about why you should keep calm and keep rolling dice.

title: Thoughts on Scenarios with 50% Lords & Heroes
description: With all the videos coming out about the 50% lords and Heroes, I thought I would post my thoughts about Scenarios. Everyone is raising the idea of Scenarios being the counter to heroes and hero spam, but there are consequences to this as well. Join me for some musings on scenarios and complexity.

title: Nagash Book and Change
description: Quick Follow up to my last video. In the comments and discussion of that video the idea of change and edition wars came up. I wanted to see if maybe I could find a silver lining to the current vitriolic discussion on various (non-Warhammer Youtubers) boards. Just my 2cp, hope everyone enjoys!﻿

title: Quick Thoughts on Nagash & Herohammer
description: Just wanted to make a quick video of my thoughts on the new Nagash Book, HeroHammer, Tomb Kings and what this bodes for the coming months.

description:

In this video, we use one of Mantic’s Halo Sangheili Major miniatures to get that slick sci-fi looking candy red for its armour. You can, of course, use this technique for blues, purples and greens. Try changing the gold to silver for a different effect. In fact, I used this very technique for my Horus Heresy Thousand Sons! We hope you enjoy this one!

title: Painting an Ultramarine Intercessor like it's the 90's!

That’s right, red guns are back, baby and they look fabulous! We also managed to scrounge an old pot of Ultramarines Blue for the job (Thanks, Joe). But it wouldn’t be a retro style video without the classic green base and we cover that too. That’s right, we went full RETRO with this one, and we hope you enjoy it as much as we enjoyed painting it. 

Tell us in the comments about your favourite era.

title: Has the art of scenery building been lost in Warhammer?
description:
Building your own scenery was a huge part of the Wargaming hobby (still is in some spheres) but with hard plastic kits and 3D printing, it's become less common. I always felt that this was one of the most fun aspects of the hobby and a great way to bring life to your gaming board. 

In this tutorial, I show you how I approach making scenery for Warhammer 40K (or any other such as Age of Sigmar, Battletech, Trench Crusade, Fallout, Star Wars and Conquest amongst others.) And the best part is, is that they can be made from trash around your house, your bitz box (most important) as well as a trip to the hardware store for really cheap components.

We will be doing a full painting tutorial for this too so keep an eye out and Subscribe to the channel for updates.

We hope you have enjoyed this video. Let us know about any cool custom scenery you have made.

Now is the time to paint this gorgeous miniature and paint it the best I can including those swirly vines. So here goes nothing...

title: The best miniature studio you've (probably) never heard of & how to paint one | Duncan Rhodes
description:
Rackham was created way back in the 1990's and were way ahead of their time in both design and miniature sculpting. They were trail blazers who created arguably the best looking miniatures, artwork and books of the time and for a short period, almost took the miniature studio crown from Games Workshop and Warhammer. In this video, we take a brief look at what made them special before unboxing a miniature I have had in my collection for over 15 years and then we paint it in all its glory.

If you enjoy painting Warhammer 40,000, Age of Sigmar, Space Marines, Old World, Moonstone, Star Wars, Fallout etc. then it's worth seeking out a few of these miniatures for a fun painting project.

title: 3 Ways to paint Dark Angels Power Armour for Warhammer 40,000 | Duncan Rhodes | Space Marines
description:
There are dozens of ways to paint Space Marine Power Armour and in this tutorial we demonstrate 3 methods to paint your Dark Angels Power Armour for Warhammer 40,000 by Games Workshop.
The first method is perfect for painting Space Marines quickly and focuses on the drybrushing technique. Here we show you different ways of using the technique to highlight the armour without making it too light. 
The second method revolves around an edge highlight technique to create sharp highlights that stand out on the tabletop.
The third technique is more advanced and uses wet blending to create more depth within the green armour. Give it a go as this technique is easier than you might think and is a great addition to your hobby arsenal. 
As we said earlier, there are tons of methods out there and these are just 3 we like to use ourselves and there are some useful techniques to learn across all three. And best of all, the methods demonstrated can be used across all Space Marine Chapters, just swap the colours to suit the appropriate Astartes chapter.

title: 4 Amazing Battle Damage Techniques for your Warhammer | 40K | Duncan Rhodes
description:
Sometimes, you might finish a model and think that it looks just a bit too clean. Freshly polished armour, gleaming paintwork - these things look great but sometimes you might want that warrior to look like he's seen some action. He may be a veteran and you want him to look the part, and that's what this video is all about!

In this video we take a painted miniature from Games Workshop's Warhammer 40,000 and show you how you can take him to hell and back. 
In this video we cover a variety of techniques that you can use to simulate damage to your troops. Whilst we use a Space Marine (Space Wolves Intercessor) for our example, the methods used are approached in such a way so as to focus on the technique rather than the particular colours so as to make this applicable to any miniature. We cover this in four segments:
1. Chipping the paint using paint, creating the optical illusion of chips and scratches etched in the armour.
2. Placing bullet holes by literally drilling and carving them into the model.
3. Adding dust kicked up around the warrior's feet by making use of weathering pigments.
4. Creating scars and wounds on the soldier's flesh.

These techniques are all great fun to use and can we used on a wide variety of miniatures from almost any game system or miniatures you like even tanks!

We hope you guys enjoy this one and remember, if you haven't already, check out our Academy over at www.duncanrhodes.com where we have almost 350, yes 350, full, indepth tutorials on there including a huge 15 part Fundamentals of Miniature Painting course included in the membership.

Cheers
Dunc & Rog

title: Fun with Colour and a Cyberpunk...just because. 😊 | Duncan Rhodes
description:
Sometimes you just wanna have some fun and do something completely different, a great way to 'cleanse your palette' when painting your miniatures. And in this video, we take a look at a method that has helped me many times over the years, the 'Blank Canvas' approach! Here I grab a miniature that I've never painted before and approach it in a completely different way by choosing a colour palette outside of my norm and I just have fun with it! I have found that this really helps me and gives me motivation and a break to continue my other projects and get them finished for those all important games and campaigns. title: 3 Ways to paint Warhammer 40,000 Space Marine Power Armour | Duncan Rhodes
description:
In this tutorial, we show you not one but three ways to paint Space Marine Power Armour for Warhammer 40,000 by Games Workshop! We start off with a technique that is perfect for speed painting so you can get your army looking good and on the tabletop in no time at all. It's also great for beginners starting their painting journey.  Then we move on to my personal go-to method for painting Space Marines, one that will make your miniatures look awesome and 'pop' on the tabletop, often labelled 'table-top standard', this method is a great way to practice and master edge highlighting. Finally, we show you a little more advanced method similar to the style of 'Eavy Metal, with some great advice on wet-blending and fine-lining. Even though we show you how to paint blue power armour, the video is all about the techniques, not the colour palette so feel free to swap around as much as you want, from Blood Angels to Imperial Fists, these techniques will have you covered. title: 4 Ways to paint RUST effects for your Warhammer 40,000, Blanchitsu and Fallout | Duncan Rhodes
description:
Metal, unfortunately, doesn't age like fine wine. But is does look amazing when it starts to rust and painting rust effects on your Warhammer, Necromunda, Blanchitsu and Fallout miniatures and scenery is a great way to add tons of character to your collection! description:
A question we are frequently asked is - "What is the difference between a wash and a contrast paint *(Citadel Contrast and Army Painter's Speed paints), and why would you choose one or the other?" There is a lot of confusion about this as these types of paint have a bit of a crossover in how they work, but there are properties unique to each that are important to know as they give very different results. This video contains lots of useful information on the subject to help you make the best choice for what techniques you like to use, and what result you want on your miniatures.

Cheers
Dunc and Rog

We start off demonstrating a speed painting method which is also fantastic for beginners and it only requires two, yes two, paints!
